claim: 19 CFR Part 134 implements the country of origin marking requirements and exceptions of section 304 of the Tariff Act.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: This part sets forth regulations implementing the country of origin marking requirements and exceptions of section 304

claim: Country of origin means the country of manufacture, production, or growth of any article of foreign origin entering the United States.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: the country of manufacture, production, or growth of any article of foreign origin entering the United States

claim: Further work or material added in another country must effect a substantial transformation to make that other country the country of origin.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: must effect a substantial transformation in order to render such other country the “country of origin”

claim: The ultimate purchaser is generally the last person in the United States who will receive the article in the form in which it was imported.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: The “ultimate purchaser” is generally the last person in the United States who will receive the article

claim: If an article is to be sold at retail in its imported form, the purchaser at retail is the ultimate purchaser.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: If an article is to be sold at retail in its imported form, the purchaser at retail is the “ultimate purchaser.”

claim: If an imported article is distributed as a gift, the recipient is the ultimate purchaser.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: If the imported article is distributed as a gift the recipient is the “ultimate purchaser”

claim: If an imported article will be used in manufacture, the manufacturer may be the ultimate purchaser if it subjects the article to a process that results in a substantial transformation.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: the manufacturer may be the “ultimate purchaser” if he subjects the imported article to a process which results in a substantial transformation
verifier_note: 19 CFR 134.1(d)(1) makes the manufacturer the ultimate purchaser only if the process results in a substantial transformation; the condition was missing. Decision row updated.

claim: If the manufacturing process is merely a minor one that leaves the identity of the imported article intact, the consumer or user of the processed article is the ultimate purchaser.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: If the manufacturing process is merely a minor one which leaves the identity of the imported article intact

claim: Every article of foreign origin must be marked in a conspicuous place as legibly, indelibly, and permanently as the nature of the article permits.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: shall be marked in a conspicuous place as legibly, indelibly, and permanently as the nature of the article

claim: Conspicuous means capable of being easily seen with normal handling of the article or container.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: capable of being easily seen with normal handling of the article or container.

claim: Articles not marked as required are subject to additional duties of 10 percent of the final appraised value.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: additional duties of 10 percent of the final appraised value

claim: The 10 percent marking duty does not apply if the articles are exported or destroyed under Customs supervision before liquidation.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: exported or destroyed under Customs supervision

claim: The marking must survive normal distribution and store handling.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: The marking must survive normal distribution and store handling.

claim: The ultimate purchaser must be able to find the marking easily and read it without strain.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: must be able to find the marking easily and read it without strain

claim: Markings must include the full English name of the country of origin.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: the markings required by this part shall include the full English name of the country of origin

claim: Abbreviations that unmistakably indicate the name of a country, such as Gt. Britain for Great Britain, are acceptable.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Abbreviations which unmistakably indicate the name of a country, such as “Gt. Britain” for “Great Britain”

claim: Stickers are an acceptable marking method when affixed in a conspicuous place so they remain on the article until it reaches the ultimate purchaser.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: they must be affixed in a conspicuous place

claim: Tags are an acceptable marking method when attached in a conspicuous place so they remain on the article until it reaches the ultimate purchaser.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: they must be attached in a conspicuous place

claim: Certain listed articles, such as knives, scissors and surgical instruments, must be marked by methods such as die stamping, cast-in-the-mold lettering or etching.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: die stamping, cast-in-the-mold lettering, etching

claim: Special marking applies when words such as United States, American or U.S.A., or the name of any city or location in the United States, appear on an article or its container and may mislead the ultimate purchaser about the actual country of origin.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: or the name of any city or location in the United States
verifier_note: 134.46 also covers names of U.S. cities or locations (and other foreign places); added because the page's example is a U.S. city name.

claim: In that case the country of origin must appear legibly and permanently in close proximity and in at least a comparable size, preceded by Made in, Product of, or other words of similar meaning.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: in close proximity to such words, letters or name, and in at least a comparable size
verifier_note: 134.46 also requires at least a comparable size; added to claim and page.

claim: When an article is excepted from marking, the outermost container in which it ordinarily reaches the ultimate purchaser must be marked.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: the outermost container or holder in which the article ordinarily reaches the ultimate purchaser shall be marked

claim: A usual container is the container in which a good will ordinarily reach its ultimate purchaser.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: a usual container means the container in which a good will ordinarily reach its ultimate purchaser.

claim: Containers treated as imported articles in their own right must be marked to indicate clearly the country of their own origin.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: shall be marked to indicate clearly the country of their own origin.

claim: Articles that are incapable of being marked are excepted from marking.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Articles that are incapable of being marked;

claim: Articles that cannot be marked before shipment to the United States without injury are excepted.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Articles that cannot be marked prior to shipment to the United States without injury;

claim: Articles that cannot be marked before shipment except at an economically prohibitive expense are excepted.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Articles that cannot be marked prior to shipment to the United States except at an expense economically prohibitive

claim: Articles for which marking the containers will reasonably indicate the origin are excepted.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Articles for which the marking of the containers will reasonably indicate the origin of the articles;

claim: Articles imported for use by the importer and not intended for sale in any form are excepted.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Articles imported for use by the importer and not intended for sale in their imported or any other form;

claim: Articles for which the ultimate purchaser must necessarily know the country of origin are excepted.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Articles for which the ultimate purchaser must necessarily know

claim: Articles produced more than 20 years before importation are excepted.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Articles which were produced more than 20 years prior to their importation into the United States;

claim: Products of the United States exported and returned are excepted.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Products of the United States exported and returned;

claim: The J-list in 19 CFR 134.33 excepts listed articles such as works of art, cigars and cigarettes, eggs, feathers and firewood.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: “Art, works of.” “Cigars and cigarettes.” “Eggs.” “Feathers.” “Firewood.”

claim: An article used in U.S. manufacture that results in an article with a different name, character, or use makes the U.S. manufacturer the ultimate purchaser, so the import is excepted, though its outermost containers must still be marked.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: An article used in the United States in manufacture which results in an article having a name, character, or use differing

claim: If a J-list article or an article incapable of being marked is intended to be repacked in new containers for sale to an ultimate purchaser after release, the importer must certify that it will mark the new containers or notify later buyers.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: If an article subject to these requirements is intended to be repacked in new containers for sale to an ultimate purchaser
verifier_note: This certification is in 134.25, headed 'Containers or holders for repacked J-list articles and articles incapable of being marked'; the claim and page stated it as applying to all repacked goods. Scope narrowed; retail repacking of marked articles is covered by 134.26 (claim -38).

claim: Under that certification, the importer must notify the purchaser or transferee in writing at the time of sale or transfer.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: the importer shall notify such purchaser or transferee, in writing, at the time of sale or transfer.

claim: The repacking certification statement must be filed with the Center director at the time of entry summary.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: The certification statement shall be filed with the Center director at the time of entry summary.

claim: When articles will be repacked in retail containers such as blister packs, the importer may certify that it will not obscure or conceal the marking on the article.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: obscure or conceal the country of origin marking appearing on the article

claim: The retail-repacking rules do not apply to a container that can readily be opened for inspection by the ultimate purchaser, unless the container bears a U.S. address or other potentially misleading marking.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: unless such container bears a U.S. address or other potentially misleading marking
verifier_note: 134.26(f) carve-out has an exception for containers bearing a U.S. address or other potentially misleading marking; added.

claim: CBP notifies the importer of a marking problem on Customs Form 4647 or its electronic equivalent.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: Customs Form 4647, or its electronic equivalent

claim: Articles in examination packages that are not exported, destroyed, or properly marked within a reasonable time, not more than 30 days, are sent to general-order storage.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register

publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: within 30 days from the date of the notice of redelivery

publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
evidence: incurred under the bond in an amount equal to the entered value

claim: Articles held for inspection will not be delivered until marked with their country of origin.
publisher: eCFR — Office of the Federal Register
